To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rhesus monkeys with lesions of the fornix are impaired in learning new conditional stimulus-response associations even if neither the stimuli nor the responses have a spatial component.

Fornix transected monkeys are impaired in learning new nonspatial conditional associations, even if the stimuli and responses are familiar, but they are not impaired in responding to familiar stimuli that are associated with already learned responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hippocampi in associative learning, particularly in learning that occurs rapidly and recently.
understanding the neural basis of associative learning.
understanding the role of the hippocampical system in learning and memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hippocampus is necessary for learning new associations, but not for performing already-learned associations, and the associations can involve any type of information, including non-spatial information.
the hippocampus is not a spatial brain, but a brain for learning.
the hippocampus plays a role in the rapid and associative acquisition of information, and this information may be spatial or nonspatial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampus is involved in learning associations that are novel, and are learned rapidly and recently, and that are not spatial in nature.
the hippocampi are necessary for learning associations between stimuli and responses that are not necessarily spatially related.
the hippocampi play an important role in learning and retaining new associations between visual stimuli and responses, even when no aspect of the association is spatially defined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampic system plays a role in associative learning beyond that of spatial learning.

the hippocampical system plays a critical role in learning new stimulus-reward associations, even when the stimulus is non-spatially defined and even when the reward is non-spatial, and even when the animal already has a history of reward associated with that stimulus.

the hippocampus is not just a brain region that is involved in memory, but rather it is a brain region that has a role in learning, and it is a brain system that is critical for the learning of associations.
